get.summary: Return a list of resource alerts
get.description:
Return a list of alerts which match specified query as either JSON or comma-separated values (CSV).

Example query to get a list of service event alerts:

https://<host>/rest/resource-alerts?query='serviceEventSource%20EQ%20%22true%22'

The table below gives an overview of the uses of the resource alerts API.

| Description                                 | Method | Content Type     | Produces |
| -----------                                 | ------ | -----            | ----     |
| Get a list of resource alerts               | GET    | application/json | JSON     |
| Get a list of resource alerts in CSV format | GET    | text/csv         | CSV      |

activityUri.description: URI of the task resource of the activity that created the alert, if the alert was caused by an operation in the appliance. Used in tracking root causes.

alertState.description: This indicates the state of an alert. Active alerts of a resource help determine its health status. Cleared alerts indicate that the alerts are no longer of concern and will not affect the health status of a resource. Locked alerts are active alerts that cannot be cleared or deleted by the user. Only the internal resource manager can change the state of the locked alert after the underlying problem is corrected. Like active alerts, locked alerts help determine the health status of a resource. The system will automatically set the state of an alert to Cleared if the severity of the alert is OK.

alertTypeID.description: Uniquely identifies the type of the alert resource. Typically this is an identifier for which the alert resource is created. For example - an alert type of Trap.cpqHo2NicStatusFailed indicates a trap where the NIC was in a failed condition. The alertTypeID is the same as the eventTypeID of the event(s) from which the alert is created.

lifeCycle.description: Life cycle alerts do not determine status of a resource. Life cycle alerts are created as a result of some activity on a resource such as powering on or off a server or inserting a blade server in an enclosure. get.description: Retrieve the web server certificate and certificate chain of the specified remote appliance.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Address of the server from which certificates are to be retrieved.

post.description:
Import the given server certificate into the appliance.
- If a leaf certificate is passed with aliasName,
it is stored in the appliance with its aliasName.
- If a leaf certificate is passed without aliasName,
it is stored in the appliance with Common Name in the certificate as aliasName.
- If a CA chain is passed, root certificate is trusted with thumbprint
provided full chain can be established with the certs passed.

The maximum allowed certificate chain depth is 10.
Appliance will not allow import of the user supplied certificate(s)
if not able to build a valid certification path.

parameters.name: Forcesaveleaf
parameters.description:
Header used to identify if the CA leaf has to be saved forcefully.
Default value is "false". List of valid input values are {"false","true"}.

parameters.name: Skip-Cert-Validation
parameters.description:
Header used to identify if certificate validations are enabled.
Default value is "false". List of valid input values are {"false","true"}.

get.description: Return a list of tasks matching the specified query.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description:
The language code requested in the response.
If a suitable match to the requested language is not available, en-US or the appliance locale is used.

parameters.name: Auth
parameters.description:
Session authorization token obtained from logging in.
If this header is not included or if the session-token is invalid, the response code will be 401 Unauthorized.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description:
The request is conditionally processed only if the current ETag for the resource
does not match the ETag passed in this header.
If the ETag specified in this header matches the resource's current ETag,
the status code returned from the GET will be 304 Not Modified.

parameters.name: X-Api-Version
parameters.description:
Specifies the version of the API to invoke.
The behavior of a given API version remains the same.
It is upward compatible from release to release.
New versions of an API are created when new features or changes are introduced.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
The number of resources to return. A count of -1 requests all the items up to the
maximum page size of 500.  The actual number of items in the response can differ
from the requested count if the sum of start and count exceed the total number of items,
or if returning the requested number of items would take too long.  If this field is
omitted, it defaults to 25.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Specifies which fields should be returned in the result set.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
A general filter/query string to narrow the list of items returned.
The default is no filter - all resources are returned.

Filter string format {attribute} {op} '{value}'
Example
  filter="name EQ 'resource1'"
  filter=name='resource1'
  filter="status IN ('OK','WARNING','ERROR')"
  filter="applianceLocation EQ '10.10.0.1' AND status IN ('OK')"

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
Query string used to filter results by resource attribute.
Query string format {attribute} {op} '{value}'
Example
  query="name EQ 'resource1'"
  query=name='resource1'
  query="status IN ('OK','WARNING','ERROR')"
  query="applianceLocation EQ '10.10.0.1' AND status IN ('OK')"

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The sort order of the returned data set. If no sort is specified the default sort is name:ascending, except for alerts resources where the default sort is created:descending.
Example
  sort=name:asc
  sort=name:ascending
  sort=name:desc
  sort=name:descending

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The first item to return, using 0-based indexing. If not specified, the default is 0 - start with the first available item.

get.description: Return an existing task identified by its unique ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The UUID of task.

associationType.description:
Type of association. In general, Task uses MANAGED_BY
associationType, as task is managed by some resource.

resourceCategory.description:
Category of the resource associated with the task (for
example, 'enclosures'), not necessarily the RM performing
the task.

resourceName.description: Display name of the resource associated with the task.

resourceUri.description: URI of the resource associated with the task.

associatedTaskURI.description:
If the current task is associated with another task, this
represents the URI of another task. And if the current task
is not associated with any other task, it signifies with NULL.

category.description: The category is used to help identify the type of resource.

completedSteps.description: Number of steps currently completed by the task.

computedPercentComplete.description:
Percent complete computed taking into account both percent
complete and expected duration of the task

created.description: Date and time when the appliance was created.

data.description:
A map of string-values containing extra/internal data defined
for the particular task, usually for internal use

eTag.description:
Entity tag/version ID of the resource, the same value that is
returned in the ETag header on a GET of the resource

expectedDuration.description:
Estimated number of seconds that the task is expected to take
to complete

hidden.description:
Boolean field indicating if the task is hidden or visible.
Default is false.
enum:
  - true
  - false

modified.description: Date when the resource was last modified

owner.description: The name of the user under whose authority the task is running

parentTaskUri.description: URI of the parent task. NULL if no parent exists.

percentComplete.description:
Percentage of task currently completed. If TaskState
of this task currently belongs to any of the TERMINAL states
(Terminated, Killed, Completed, Error, or Warning), percentComplete
and computedPercentComplete will be set to 100.

statusUpdate.description:
Text containing update that the service logged during
execution of the task

timestamp.description: Date and time when the progress update was logged

stateReason.description: Contains the reason for changing to current state of the task

taskErrors.description: Error messages associated with the task

data.description: Contains extra data defined for the particular error

details.description: Optional verbose description of the error with additional information

errorCode.description:
A string code which uniquely identifies the specific error allowing
clients to switch on specific errors without having to parse the error message

errorSource.description: A reference to the resource or attribute that applies to an error

nestedErrors.description: An array of task errors used when there are multiple errors

recommendedActions.description: A description of what can be done to rectify the problem

taskOutput.description: Output resulting from the running of the task

taskStatus.description: Short summary of the current execution/completion status

totalSteps.description: Total number of steps to be completed for this task

type.description: Uniquely identifies the type of the JSON object.

uri.description: The canonical URI of the resource

userInitiated.description:
If the task is the result of a user initiated command it is TRUE.
Otherwise it is FALSE.
